question.problem:
A random variable $X$ has the probability distribution given below.

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{1}{6}$ | $\frac{1}{12}$ | $\frac{5}{12}$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $\frac{1}{12}$ |

Calculate $\text{E}[4X-8].$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's find $\text{E}[X].$ 

The expected value of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ and sample space $S$ is given by

$$
\text{E}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x).
$$

Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & ={\sum }_{x\in S}x\cdot f(x) \\  & =0\cdot \frac{1}{6}+1\cdot \frac{1}{12}+2\cdot \frac{5}{12}+3\cdot \frac{1}{4}+4\cdot \frac{1}{12} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[4X-8] & =4\text{E}[X]-8 \\  & =4\cdot 2-8 \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
